course_name_original: Análisis y Diseño de Procesos Químicos
course_name_en: Analysis and Design of Chemical Processes
prerequisites: Admission to the Master's in Industrial Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the main characteristics of the chemical industry and become familiar with the specific terminology of this type of industrial processes.
Formulate and solve process design problems by using material and energy balances in systems with and without chemical reaction.
Understand the stages in the design of a process that integrates economic, safety, and environmental concepts.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to processes, unit operations and transport phenomena.

Material balances. Resolution of balances in: systems without chemical reaction, systems with chemical reaction, multi-stage and multi-unit systems. Recirculations, bypass, purges and industrial application of material balances.
Energy balances. Systems without chemical reaction. Systems with chemical reaction. Energy effects of non-ideality.
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, students must not achieve less than 30% of the grade assigned to the theoretical-practical part of the exam, and not less than 30% of the grade assigned to the problem-solving part of the exam. The final evaluation grade cannot be less than 40% of its maximum value. In other calls, the final grade will be calculated with the grades from Classroom Practices and Group Tutorials obtained during the last period the subject was taught, and the grade obtained in the final evaluation for that call. For differentiated evaluation, a final exam worth 100% of the final grade will be conducted.
